issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as type double, while the solution implementation declares these attributes as int. This creates a cross-artifact and intra-specification type mismatch (problem UML vs solution code and problem UML internally vs method return types) that can confuse students about which numeric type to use and whether methods like getTotalNumberOfStudents should return an int or a double.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the UML and problem text to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (recommended, since counts are integral) so the solution and methods (returning int) match the specification, or (B) change the template and solution attributes to double and update method signatures/return types (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents -> double and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor -> double) and documentation to reflect floating-point counts.
